meta.title: Trattoria Il Pavone | Traditional Bassano cuisine since 1941
meta.description: Historic trattoria in Romano d'Ezzelino, near Bassano del Grappa. Since 1941: Bassano-style asparagus and eggs, grilled meat, fresh pasta and Vicenza-style salt cod. Book online.

kitchen.title: Our Cuisine
kitchen.lead: Typical local cooking, grilled meat and fresh pasta. Trattoria il Pavone is known as the sanctuary of asparagus, a name rooted in the Venetian tradition its chefs have always respected.
kitchen.closing: Dishes made with typical seasonal ingredients, such as Treviso radicchio, DOC asparagus from Bassano del Grappa, Vicenza-style salt cod and our renowned grilled meat.

antipasti.title: Starters and panari
antipasti.text: Starters served on “panari”, literally polenta boards, paired with seasonal Venetian produce. The “prince” of starters is without doubt the panaro del Pavone, where tradition and culinary imagination come together.
antipasti.alt: Aubergine and cheese starter served on a slate plate in the dining room

pasta.title: Fresh pasta
pasta.text: Homemade pasta and sauces prepared with the care and passion of those who love this work.
pasta.alt: Bigoli, the long pasta typical of the Veneto

risotti.title: Risotto
risotti.text: Excellent risottos, made with seasonal ingredients such as Treviso radicchio and pumpkin.
risotti.alt: Radicchio risotto served on a white plate

carne.title: Grilled meat
carne.text: Il Pavone takes particular pride in its grilled meat. Carefully selected cuts are aged to the right point and cooked strictly over embers, which give every dish its added value.
carne.alt: Sliced grilled beef with rosemary and polenta

asparagi.title: Bassano-style asparagus and eggs
asparagi.text: A story of its own. Since the very early 1940s Il Pavone has served this delicacy, inspired by farming tradition, becoming a point of reference for lovers of the white asparagus of Bassano.
asparagi.alt: Two bundles of white Bassano asparagus tied with willow, with eggs, in front of the fireplace

baccala.title: Vicenza-style salt cod
baccala.text: Not to be forgotten is the baccalà: Vicenza-style, creamed on the panaro and in the tasting trio.
baccala.alt: Vicenza-style salt cod with polenta on the plate

dolci.title: Desserts
dolci.text: Desserts bring every gathering to a worthy close: from grandmother's simple little sweets to creations that will amaze you with the imagination of their presentation.
dolci.alt: Two flambéed crema catalana served at the table

story.title: Our Story
story.staffAlt: The staff of Trattoria Il Pavone in front of the old wall of the villa
story.wallAlt: Dining room wall with fresco and fabric lamps

chapters.text: The story of “Trattoria il Pavone” begins when the Lunardon family moved, in 1939, into what had been the historic country villa of a distinguished citizen of Bassano who lived at the turn of the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries: Jacopo Vittorelli.

A much admired writer and poet, he owned a vast estate on which a Renaissance villa had stood. It was completely destroyed, but he kept some of its drawings. The maestro decided to rebuild a country residence based on those drawings, which explains the building's neoclassical style rather than the Baroque that the fashion of the time would have suggested.

On his death, as was customary, he left the entire property to a priest of his time, Don Pirani, who nobly took in the orphan girls of the Bassano area. Before he died, Vittorelli arranged for Don Pirani's orphans to spend holidays at his country villa, which it seems continued regularly until the first half of the twentieth century.
Turned into a trattoria in 1941, “il Pavone” offered its guests the fruits of farm labour, and from this came the most traditional dish of Bassano's gastronomy: asparagus and eggs.
Having become the “sanctuary” of asparagus par excellence, the current management has enriched the menu with variations that satisfy today's tastes and needs.

This, in short, is the story of “il Pavone”, witness to many other human events, from the brigands who took refuge within its walls to the soldiers who, passing through, left dedications to their sweethearts written in 1860 and still visible today: in short, a place rich in history, charm and flavour.
